reason: Recording-order artifact of a Ruby splat argument: logger.rb:23-24 writes `logger.push_tags(*compute_tags(request))`, so the extractor records push_tags before its own argument, while TS evaluates computeTags(request) first. Same call set, same order at run time.

Recording-order artifact of a Ruby block argument: logger.rb:39 writes `logger.info { started_request_message(request) }`, so the extractor records info first, while TS evaluates the message eagerly as info's argument — RackLoggerLike#info takes the string, not a thunk.
